packs.framework: OWASP Agentic Skills Top 10 with OWASP Agentic Applications 2026 related taxonomy
packs.selection_scope: All ten skill-layer risks are dispositioned; the broader ASI release is pinned only as stable related context.

items.label: Malicious Skills
items.claim: The checked-in inert pilot exercises malicious-skill instruction patterns as infrastructure validation; it is not hidden-corpus efficacy evidence or a safety finding.

items.label: Supply Chain Compromise
items.claim: The evaluation candidate binds an exact GitHub commit, retained bytes, and a bounded source-reference graph.

items.label: Over-Privileged Skills
items.claim: Declared-versus-observed permissions require the deep-analysis and runtime-policy phases; Phase 0 makes no enforcement claim.

items.label: Insecure Metadata
items.claim: Current ingestion is bounded, schema validated, and fail closed on malformed machine contracts.

items.label: Untrusted External Instructions
items.claim: The Phase 0 candidate inventories literal external references and preserves unresolved references without treating them as approved.

items.label: Weak Isolation
items.claim: One isolated benchmark smoke validates handoff plumbing, but supported analyzer isolation is not earned until the deep-analysis phase.

items.label: Update Drift
items.claim: Evaluation acquisition and baseline identities are immutable and digest bound; install and update enforcement remain Phase 1.

items.label: Poor Scanning
items.claim: The burden-constrained benchmark compares pinned scanners and Aragorn under one evidence-verifying contract; efficacy remains unproven until the hidden run passes.

items.label: No Governance
items.claim: Decisions, policy identity, source identity, and evidence are retained as machine-readable records; this is not organizational governance certification.

items.label: Cross-Platform Reuse
items.claim: Phase 0 is intentionally bounded to GitHub Agent Skills; cross-platform adapters require later upstream-integration evidence.

packs.selection_scope: Nine ATLAS techniques selected for agent-skill and MCP acquisition, instruction manipulation, credential access, unsafe invocation, and exfiltration; not the full ATLAS matrix.

items.label: Publish Poisoned AI Agent Tool
items.claim: The threat is included in the acquisition threat model; Aragorn evaluates post-publication acquisition and does not claim registry prevention or hidden-corpus coverage from this mapping.

items.label: AI Agent Tool
items.claim: Exact source and analyzer component identities are retained for the bounded acquisition evaluation.

items.label: Poisoned AI Agent Tool
items.claim: Inert poisoned-tool content can be evaluated without activating it as an agent capability.

items.label: Indirect
items.claim: The checked-in inert pilot includes an indirect hidden-instruction pattern; this validates fixture and protocol handling only. The parent is AML.T0051 LLM Prompt Injection.

items.label: LLM Prompt Obfuscation
items.claim: The checked-in pilot declares an obfuscated zero-width pattern and the protocol can carry it into the future burden-constrained run; no hidden result exists yet.

items.label: AI Agent Tool Poisoning
items.claim: Aragorn inventories acquired content and referenced artifacts before activation; complete recursive closure remains a Phase 1 gate.

items.label: AI Agent Tool Invocation
items.claim: Pre-install analysis cannot establish live least-privilege invocation; enforcement and containment are runtime Phase 3 properties.

items.label: AI Agent Tool Credential Harvesting
items.claim: Checked-in inert fixtures exercise credential-harvesting intent detection without containing live credentials.

items.label: Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation
items.claim: Checked-in inert fixtures exercise exfiltration intent detection; blocking a protected sink is reserved for the runtime exit gate.

packs.framework: NIST AI RMF 1.0 and Generative AI Profile
packs.selection_scope: Seven fixed GenAI Profile actions spanning GOVERN, MAP, MEASURE, and MANAGE for acquisition due diligence and Phase 0 evaluation.

sources.title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework AI RMF 1.0
Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework Generative Artificial Intelligence Profile

items.label: Minimum assurance thresholds and go or no-go approval
items.claim: Phase 0 predeclares held-out recall improvement and benign-intervention thresholds before the hidden run.

items.label: Acquisition due diligence for third-party GAI tools
items.claim: The design treats public skills and scanner dependencies as third-party supply-chain inputs with pinned identity and bounded acquisition.

items.label: Profile threats, negative impacts, vulnerabilities, and likelihood
items.claim: The architecture records the trust boundary, principal failure modes, and residual limitations for the acquisition use case.

items.label: Evaluate capability claims with empirically validated methods
items.claim: As a framework-informed analogy to model capability claims, Aragorn separates infrastructure smoke from its tool-efficacy claim and requires retained evidence for both.

items.label: Assess baseline security concerns including compromised dependencies and autonomous agents
items.claim: The threat model and acquisition candidate address compromised third-party dependencies and autonomous-agent inputs; this mapping does not establish complete security or resilience.

items.label: Adversarial security and prompt-injection testing
items.claim: The checked-in inert pilot and label-blind protocol support adversarial instruction testing; the full frozen hidden comparison has not run.

items.label: Document release trade-offs and disposition risks above tolerance
items.claim: The roadmap keeps Aragorn private, defines kill criteria, and does not permit Phase 0 evidence to authorize installation.

limitations: This gate is a scoped standards crosswalk, not certification, compliance, or exhaustive framework coverage.
A mapped item means a claim has a repository evidence or roadmap reference; it does not mean the risk is fully mitigated.
The gate does not demonstrate independent human authorship, design-partner adoption, usability, or external product review.
The gate does not replace the burden-constrained hidden-corpus efficacy thresholds.
The gate does not establish production isolation, runtime containment, exact-digest installation, or agent-capability EDR status.
The OWASP Agentic Skills source is an active-development draft pinned to one exact commit.
Independent human security review remains a Phase 5 release requirement.
